author: Nate Miller
title: Matt Seelinger moved to Mets
desc: Matt Seelinger was traded to the Mets on Monday.
impact: The Tigers will receive cash considerations in exchange for Seelinger. The 31-year-old righty has spent all of this season at the Triple-A level so far, posting a respectable 3.89 ERA with 49 strikeouts across 39 1/3 innings.

author: Nate Miller
title: Woo-Suk Go dealt to Twins
desc: Woo-Suk Go was traded to the Twins on Sunday.
impact: Go has spent the season pitching between Double-A and Triple-A in the Tigers system so far. Over 27 relief appearances, he has posted an impressive 1.96 ERA with 54 strikeouts across 41 1/3 innings. The Korean righty will report to the club on Tuesday.

author: Nate Miller
title: Michael Harris II drives in three Sunday
desc: Michael Harris II went 2-for-5 with a pair of singles, three RBI, and a run scored in Sunday's 10-9 loss to the Mets.
impact: The Mets' pitching staff just has not been able to figure Harris out over the last three days. The dynamic center fielder has come up with multiple hits in each of the last three games, going 7-for-14 with two homers, seven RBI, and four runs scored. Harris is in the middle of a sensational season that has him sporting an .840 OPS with 16 long balls and 51 RBI through 82 games.

author: Nate Miller
title: Drake Baldwin clubs first career grand slam
desc: Drake Baldwin went 2-for-4 with a grand slam and two runs scored in Sunday's 10-9 loss to the Mets.
impact: Baldwin is trying to put a dreadful slump behind him, and he went a long way toward doing that Sunday. The second-year catcher belted the first grand slam of his career during a wild ninth inning in Atlanta, giving him his first homer in nearly three weeks. Baldwin has shown improvement at the plate since moving to the lead-off spot, as he has reached base nine times and scored six runs over his last six games.

author: Nate Miller
title: Aaron Nola turns in solid effort Sunday
desc: Aaron Nola gave up three runs on seven hits and no walks while striking out seven over seven innings in Sunday's 5-2 loss to the Royals.
impact: Nola bounced back from a rough outing against the Pirates on Monday. Unfortunately for the veteran righty, the Philly bats didn't offer him much support. Nola has been a rollercoaster of inconsistency this season, posting a 5.87 ERA through 18 starts. He has recorded 94 strikeouts across 92 innings, however. Given Nola's long track record of solid pitching, he's at least worth keeping an eye on as a potential second-half sleeper.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Bo Bichette drives in three in win
desc: Bo Bichette went 3-for-5 with a double and three RBI in Sunday's 10-9 win over the Braves. His two-run double in the ninth inning traveled 407 feet to center field and helped extend New York's lead before Atlanta rallied in the bottom half.
impact: Bichette is batting .350 with five home runs, eight doubles, and 22 RBI over his last 29 games.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Nolan McLean earns win over Braves
desc: Nolan McLean picked up the win Sunday after allowing three runs, two earned, over six-plus innings against Atlanta. All three runs came in the first inning, with the unearned run coming after McLean's errant pickoff throw. He struck out five and walked one before exiting in the seventh after allowing a leadoff single to Austin Riley.
impact: McLean has won four of his last five decisions and is now 6-5 with a 3.73 ERA. He owns a 30:6 K over his last four starts and is scheduled to face the Red Sox on Friday.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Devin Williams records 13th save
desc: Devin Williams earned the save Sunday against Atlanta after allowing one run over two-thirds of an inning. He entered with one out and the bases empty after Drake Baldwin hit a grand slam off Huascar Brazoban, then struck out Ozzie Albies before allowing three straight hits. Williams ended the game by striking out Dominic Smith with the winning run on second base.
impact: Williams has converted 13 of his 14 save chances this season. He needed 22 pitches Sunday but had four days off entering the outing, leaving him likely available Monday.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: A.J. Ewing homers against Braves
desc: A.J. Ewing went 2-for-4 with a home run Sunday against the Braves. After sitting against a left-hander Saturday, Ewing started versus Martín Pérez and took him deep for his fifth major-league homer.
impact: Ewing is hitting .222/.280/.444 in 45 at-bats against lefties, compared to .281/.370/.391 in 121 at-bats versus right-handers. He batted seventh Sunday but is likely to return to the leadoff spot against right-hander Reynaldo López on Monday.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Ezequiel Duran goes deep in loss
desc: Ezequiel Duran went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 6-3 loss to the Tigers. He cut into Detroit's lead in the eighth inning with his seventh homer of the season, taking Drew Anderson deep.
impact: Duran is batting .353 with an .802 OPS over his last nine games. He is slashing .273/.323/.418 with seven home runs, 15 doubles, two triples, 44 RBI, 35 runs, and six stolen bases across 301 plate appearances this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jake Burger blasts 15th homer
desc: Jake Burger went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 6-3 loss to the Tigers. He opened the scoring in the third inning by taking Casey Mize deep for his 15th homer of the season.
impact: Burger is 2-for-24 over his last six games despite Sunday's long ball. He is slashing .246/.309/.432 with 14 doubles, 15 home runs, 53 RBI, 39 runs, and two stolen bases across 86 games this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Kumar Rocker takes loss to Tigers
desc: Kumar Rocker took the loss Sunday against the Tigers after allowing three runs on five hits and one walk over 4.1 innings. He struck out four. Most of the damage came on a two-run homer by Riley Greene in the fourth inning, and Rocker exited in the fifth after allowing a single.
impact: It was Rocker's shortest outing since May 8. He owns a 3.95 ERA, 1.34 WHIP, and 74:32 K across 84.1 innings and is scheduled to face the Astros at home in his next start.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Aroldis Chapman records 18th save
desc: Aroldis Chapman picked up the save in Sunday's 7-5 win over the Angels, allowing a solo home run while striking out two over one inning. Zach Neto took him deep with two outs before Chapman struck out the next batter to secure his 18th save of the season.
impact: Chapman has allowed six earned runs over six innings across his last seven appearances, taking two losses while converting four of six save chances during that stretch. He owns a 2.36 ERA, 1.27 WHIP, and 35:12 K across 26.2 innings this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Willson Contreras crushes 20th homer
desc: Willson Contreras went 1-for-4 with a three-run home run and a walk in Sunday's 7-5 win over the Angels. He launched a 446-foot homer to left field in the third inning, giving Boston a lead it kept the rest of the way.
impact: Contreras has matched last season's total of 20 home runs and is on pace to surpass his career high of 24, set in 2019. He is slashing .284/.378/.542 with 37 extra-base hits, 59 RBI, 45 runs, and two stolen bases across 86 games.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jarren Duran snaps homerless streak in win
desc: Jarren Duran went 2-for-3 with a two-run home run and a walk in Sunday's 7-5 win over the Angels. He put Boston on the board with a two-run shot in the second inning, ending a 15-game homerless stretch in which he went 4-for-50.
impact: Duran is slashing .197/.259/.361 with 13 home runs, 43 RBI, 39 runs, and 14 stolen bases across 81 games. He has remained Boston's primary left fielder despite his offensive struggles, though Nate Eaton continues to take some playing time against left-handed pitching.
